title: Research
text:
Groundwater & water policy

How California manages groundwater under SGMA, how watersheds respond to dams
and overdraft, and how coastal communities plan with nature-based solutions.


  Jun 2026 – present
  
    Groundwater Accounting Landscape Analysis
    Groundwater Policy Intern · Environmental Defense Fund · funded by California DWR
    Leading a policy and literature landscape analysis to inform a statewide Groundwater Accounting Platform.
    I synthesized 65 peer-reviewed papers and 65+ groundwater plans, rules, and reports (20,000+ pages) from six
    subbasins, coding 690+ quote-verified findings on stream depletion, multi-benefit land repurposing, and
    community equity that inform best-practice recommendations to DWR.
    SGMAGroundwaterPolicy analysisPython
     Interactive portfolio site
  



  Mar – Jun 2026
  
    Merced River Watershed Analysis
    Bren School · Watershed Analysis
    An integrated characterization of the 3,300 km² Merced River system, covering flow regime alteration,
    sediment transport, and lower-reach channel geomorphology. Flow-duration and flood-frequency curves show an
    80% reduction in mean annual flood from dam operations and permanent sediment immobility in the lower reach.
    HydrologyGeomorphologyR
  



  Sep – Dec 2025
  
    Salinas River Watershed: Sustainable Water Management Plan
    Bren School · Groundwater Management
    Synthesized climate, hydrologic, land-use, population, and water-use data into a management plan for the
    Salinas River Watershed. Recommendations integrate recharge enhancement, irrigation-efficiency analysis, and
    land-use-specific BMPs to reduce overdraft and support SGMA compliance.
    SGMAArcGIS ProR
     Read the plan (PDF)
  



  Jan – Mar 2025
  
    Coastal Dune Restoration in Sea-Level Rise Planning
    UCSB Geography · Policy content analysis
    A systematic content analysis of 55 California sea-level rise adaptation plans, each coded into a
    27-variable dataset. About 95% of jurisdictions mention dunes, but most engage only at a low level, and
    native planting is proposed nearly 4× as often as invasive removal. I developed a
    "recognition–action gap" framework from these findings and paired it with ArcGIS mapping of historic dune
    extent, NOAA inundation projections, and CalEnviroScreen to prioritize restoration that protects
    disadvantaged communities.
    Coastal adaptationNature-based solutionsArcGIS
  



  Sep – Dec 2024
  
    SGMA, Biodiversity & Multi-benefit Land Repurposing
    Bren School · Group research
    A literature review and seven expert interviews (NGOs, agencies, nonprofits) on how SGMA-driven fallowing
    affects biodiversity, and on the incentives for multi-benefit land repurposing in the Central Valley.
    I presented the findings to about 80 graduate students and an industry panel.
    SGMALand repurposingInterviews
  




  
  Irrigation & remote sensing

Seeing irrigation from space, from smallholder plots in Zambia to the croplands of the
Western U.S., and asking what it does for crops, water, and climate.


  Nov 2024 – Aug 2026
  
    Mapping Dry-Season Smallholder Irrigation in Zambia
    Graduate Research Assistant · Water, Vegetation & Society (WAVES) Lab, UCSB · with Anna Boser & Kelly Caylor
    
      Designed a satellite image labeling protocol and led 4 undergraduates to label 2,325 images at 933 locations,
      building a benchmark ML dataset. Irrigation appeared at 27% of sites, about 400 km² with no prior record.
      Engineered an HPC pipeline (SLURM, Earth Engine, Python) that has downloaded 1.4M+ Sentinel-2 time-series
      stacks (50M+ images) for 188K locations over 10 years, with job recovery and QA checks.
      Spent summer 2025 in Lusaka with the University of Zambia. I built an R Shiny data explorer for local
      stakeholders, gave three seminars, and held ten meetings with researchers, NGOs, and government officials.
    
    IrrigationSentinel-2Machine learningHPCShiny
     Code in a private lab repository
  



  Aug 2025 – present
  
    Does Irrigation Buffer Crops Against Drought?
    Independent research · UCSB Geography · advisor: Zoe Pierrat
    Isolating the human contribution to evapotranspiration by comparing OpenET satellite-derived ET with NLDAS
    modeled ET across Western U.S. croplands, to estimate consumptive water use and aquifer drawdown. Using
    solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence (SIF) across 434,000+ pixel-months (2015–2024), I find that irrigation
    buffers crop photosynthesis under moderate drought, with 83.7% of irrigated pixels showing a positive
    buffering signal, but loses effectiveness under severe drought.
    EvapotranspirationSIFOpenETPython · xarray
     SIF analysis code
  



  Jan 2025 – present
  
    Coast Live Oak Drought Physiology
    Field volunteer researcher · WAVES Lab · Jack and Laura Dangermond Preserve
    Measuring stomatal conductance of Coast Live Oaks to track physiological responses to drought, supporting
    the Earth Research Institute's work on predicting ecosystem resilience.
    EcophysiologyFieldwork
  




  
  Multifunctional landscapes

Land that does more than one job: growing food under solar panels or among trees, and
where those systems make sense as the climate shifts.


  Oct 2025 – Sep 2026
  
    Agroforestry & Agrivoltaic Suitability Across Sub-Saharan Africa (SPARCLE)
    Arnhold Graduate Fellow · Larsen Lab (UCSB) & Conservation International
    Built continental-scale R geospatial pipelines that harmonize 10+ climate, soil, land-cover, and
    socioeconomic layers at 1 km to map suitability for agroforestry and agrivoltaic systems under current
    conditions and two climate scenarios (SSP1-2.6, SSP3-7.0). Quantified crop-yield co-benefits under shading and
    electricity-generation potential. Led a submission-ready manuscript for Environmental Research Letters
    with faculty advisors and Conservation International.
    AgroforestryAgrivoltaicsMulti-criteria analysisR · terraCHELSA
     Repository private until publication
  



  Jan – Mar 2025
  
    Global Intercropping Meta-Analysis Explorer
    Bren School · Team project
    An interactive R Shiny app for a global meta-analysis of intercropping experiments, with map, time-series,
    and crop-pair views and a PCA on land-equivalent-ratio metrics to find drivers of yield gains and input
    reductions.
    AgroecologyShinyPCA
     Code
  




  
  Conservation & climate risk

Spatial analysis in support of the people and organizations protecting land, from
Indigenous territories in Amazonia to chaparral in the Los Padres.


  Apr 2025 – Jun 2026
  
    Climate Risk & Indigenous Territories in Amazonia
    Data Manager · Master's group project with Conservation International's Global IPLC Center · advisor: Bruce Kendall
    Assessed how climate risks intersect with Indigenous Peoples' and Local Communities' territories across
    Amazonia and what that means for irrecoverable carbon and biodiversity. Built ArcGIS Pro and R models to
    identify territories suited to conservation and restoration based on land use, land-cover transitions, and
    ecological climate-buffering properties, within a rights-based framework aimed at 30×30 and COP30 in Belém.
    AmazoniaClimate justiceArcGIS ProR · prioritizr
     Group repository (private)
  



  Dec 2024 – Jun 2025
  
    Fuel-Reduction Impacts & Redshanks Habitat
    Conservation Intern · Los Padres ForestWatch
    GIS habitat and vegetation analyses evaluating the ecological impacts of proposed U.S. Forest Service
    fuel-reduction projects, producing spatial layers to support conservation-focused alternatives, plus a
    distribution analysis of Adenostoma sparsifolium (Redshanks) for climate adaptation planning.
    ChaparralArcGIS ProR
     GIS processing code
  



  Aug – Sep 2024
  
    Kiwi Conservation, Whakatāne
    Volunteer · Whakatāne Kiwi Project, New Zealand
    Maintained 18 predator traps in native bush to curb non-native predators (rats, stoats, ferrets) and located
    kiwi chicks by radio telemetry to build geospatial maps of the population.
    WildlifeTelemetry

title: JacksonColdiron
text:
Environmental Scientist · Water · Land · Remote Sensing
      JacksonColdiron
      
        I study how water, agriculture, and land systems are changing, using satellite
        remote sensing, geospatial modeling, and policy analysis, and I build tools that put
        that evidence in the hands of the people who manage them.
      
      Research 
      CV
      Get in touch
    
    
      
    
  







  
    
      About
      Data science for water, food, and the landscapes in between
      
        My work sits at the intersection of water resources,
        climate-smart agriculture, and conservation planning.
        I map irrigation from space, model where multifunctional landscapes like agroforestry
        and agrivoltaics can work, and translate groundwater science into policy.
      
      
        I hold a Master of Environmental Science & Management from UC Santa Barbara's
        Bren School (Water Resource Management, 4.00 GPA).
        I'm currently a Groundwater Policy Intern at the
        Environmental Defense Fund, where I lead a landscape
        analysis for California DWR's Groundwater Accounting project. Before that I was an
        Arnhold Graduate Fellow with Conservation International and the Larsen Lab, and a
        research assistant in UCSB's Water, Vegetation & Society Lab, where I mapped
        smallholder irrigation across Zambia.
      
      
        Before Bren I worked on sustainability partnerships in New York, farmed in Colombia,
        worked with California native plants at a nursery in Oakland, and tracked kiwi chicks by radio telemetry
        in New Zealand. I bring that field-level curiosity to every dataset.
